idea: Per-puzzle merge of all public outputs
how: replay 19 public files, keep the shortest valid program per puzzle
why: the best public file already contains the shortest program for every puzzle

how: liveness pass on the final programs
why: the public pipeline already removes dead code

idea: Exact tree re-synthesis of each target (depth <= 3)
how: delete the target's exclusive cone, search all 1-3 instruction trees over the live registers, splice, replay
why: public programs are locally tight; and the cone leaves are often overwritten before the target (see E07)

idea: Move leaf targets to their cheapest position
how: same search at every position 0..N for targets nobody reads later
why: register contents at other positions are no richer for that target

how: x op y with x in the 1-step set and y in the 2-step set, plus two chain shapes
why: no target with a cone of >= 5 instructions is reachable in 4 from the live registers

how: reuse of intermediates (x*x, x+x, v2 op v1); depth 5 as A op B with A,B 2-step DAG values
why: same as E05; trees undercount sharing, DAGs did not change the answer

how: can the search rebuild each target at its original cost?
result: k=2: 77/88, k=3: 58/74, k=4: 33/64 (with all insertion positions)
why: cone leaves are overwritten mid-cone, so no single position holds them all: a local 'no gain' is not a proof of optimality

how: keep the prefix, rebuild the last 2-14 targets cheapest-first with the exact <= 4 search
why: fails whenever a target needs >= 5 instructions; when it succeeds it ties the original

idea: Are targets a few operations from earlier targets?
how: for each practice target: exact <= 4 search from start values + all smaller targets
why: the generator does not chain targets; shared family = clusters around a hidden base

how: from the live registers after the 10th target: exact <= 4 or A*B +- r with A,B,r of 0-2 steps
why: the public plans win by sharing intermediates across targets; per-target search cannot find much

how: Nilanjan_Saha123's rebuilder with beam 8..128, 30..64 targets, cut every 1-4 positions
why: full 1000-puzzle run and multi-start from 1612 near-best alternatives are the next step

idea: Joint cut of a shared helper and all its consumers
how: remove a helper value with every consumer, rebuild each consumer without it (exact search <= 5) at its own position
why: right idea (Atakan Aldemir found 21 instructions this way with a deeper reverse search), but a depth-5 exact engine is too shallow to price the rebuilt consumers

how: the extended suffix rebuilder (beam 16, every 3rd cut) run on 1,616 distinct public programs within +3 of the best, in 962 puzzles
why: the public alternatives end in the same or worse local optima; the frontier programs are robust to this rebuilder

how: remove two targets and every instruction only they need, rebuild both at the end with the reverse beam (both orders)
why: rebuilding at the end loses the register state the original program had at the targets' positions

idea: Dictionary = base B and its powers
how: same sequential planner (public reverse beam, 48 registers, dictionary pinned) with B = 2^8, 2^12, 2^16, 2^20 or the largest start value and all powers B^k <= value_limit preloaded; setup counted
result: worse than no dictionary by +44 to +168 instructions over 10 puzzles; better in only 0-2 of 10
why: the beam already reduces t = q*m + r over thousands of catalog values; a handful of powers adds almost nothing and their setup is never repaid

idea: Helper-group joint rebuild at the cheapest positions
how: for every computed value, take all targets whose recipe uses it (2-5), drop them together with everything only they need, re-insert each with the reverse beam at its cheapest position (every 2nd cut, beam 32), live values pinned
why: the first idea that touches shared helpers and keeps the register state of the original positions; rebuilding at the end of the program always failed

idea: Hidden structure between targets (continued fractions / approximate common divisors)
how: best small-denominator relation tj ~ (p/q) ti for every target pair; then an optimistic splice test for the 6,338 strong pairs (>= 12 bits) the best programs do not use
result: 10,456 strong pairs, 39% already used; optimistic gain of the unused ones: 0
why: the structure is real (shared family: 9.3% of pairs > 10 bits vs 1.4% noise) but every unused relation costs at least as much as the existing recipe
